source.citation: Written for Blackout, 2026-10-09, from the ABFM 2025 In-Training Examination critiques, items 126 to 138. Each question cites its item. Authoring batch for the ITE pool; review before trusting.

questions.q: Two weeks of green sputum and a cough that stops sleep, afebrile, no wheeze. What reduces the cough most?
questions.why: Acute bronchitis is viral and self-limited, and dextromethorphan, guaifenesin and honey are the three things shown to cut cough frequency. Codeine adds side effects without benefit, and purulent sputum does not make it bacterial.

questions.q: By about how much do antibiotics shorten the cough of acute bronchitis?
questions.why: A measurable but negligible gain, outweighed by side effects, which is why antibiotics are not recommended even though they are often prescribed. The illness itself runs two to three weeks.

questions.q: When is an albuterol inhaler appropriate in acute bronchitis?
d: When the cough passes two weeks
questions.why: Beta-agonists help the wheezing patient and no one else. Sleep loss and a long course are the normal shape of bronchitis, not reasons for a bronchodilator.

questions.q: After an ankle inversion injury, which findings call for a radiograph under the Ottawa rules?
a: Bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of the lateral malleolus
Bone tenderness at the posterior edge or tip of the medial malleolus
Bone tenderness at the base of the fifth metatarsal
Inability to bear weight for four steps
d: Bone tenderness at the anterior edge of the lateral malleolus
Bone tenderness at the base of the fourth metatarsal
questions.why: The rule is built on the bones that fracture, so the posterior malleolar edges count and the anterior edge does not. A positive rule means a weight-bearing foot and ankle film.

questions.q: Under the Ottawa ankle rules, inability to bear weight for how many steps indicates a radiograph?
questions.why: Four steps, immediately after the injury or in the clinic. Swelling on its own, however impressive, is not a criterion.

questions.q: A 13-year-old with fewer than two stools a week, painful, large enough to clog the toilet; growth and labs normal. Next step?
questions.why: He meets three Rome IV criteria for functional constipation, and polyethylene glycol has good evidence in children and adolescents. Probiotics have none, and imaging or endoscopy wait for red flags he does not have.

questions.q: Which features are Rome IV criteria for functional constipation in a child?
a: Two or fewer stools a week
Stools large enough to clog the toilet
d: Abdominal pain that wakes the child at night
questions.why: Faecal incontinence and a rectal mass complete the list. Blood, weight loss and night pain are the red flags that turn a functional diagnosis into a work-up.

questions.q: A 45-year-old smoker with diabetes, LDL 120, triglycerides 300, ten-year risk 8.2%. Which statin?
questions.why: Diabetes at 40 to 75 earns at least a moderate-intensity statin without a risk calculation, and his smoking and triglycerides push him to high intensity, which atorvastatin 40 to 80 is. Simvastatin 40 is moderate, pravastatin 20 is low, and ezetimibe is never first.

questions.q: Months of burning and numbness in the sole after an ankle sprain, pain behind the medial malleolus, Tinel positive at the ankle. Diagnosis?
questions.why: The tibial nerve is trapped under the flexor retinaculum, often after an injury. Plantar fasciitis hurts with the first steps of the morning at the medial calcaneal tuberosity, not behind the malleolus.

questions.q: Which examination finding is most helpful for diagnosing tarsal tunnel syndrome?
questions.a: A positive Tinel sign at the ankle
d: Pain with the first steps of the morning
A bruise-like pain in the centre of the heel
questions.why: There is no gold-standard test, so the tap behind the medial malleolus carries the diagnosis, with nerve studies to confirm. The three distractor findings belong to plantar fasciitis, Achilles tendinopathy and heel pad syndrome.

questions.q: A patient shoots rifles competitively. Which safety advice is right?
questions.a: Electronic hearing protection that amplifies quiet sounds
questions.why: A gunshot exceeds 140 dB and one can cause permanent loss, and electronic muffs block the shot while letting range commands through. Noise-cancelling headphones do not reduce enough, loose clothing traps hot brass, and only certified safety glasses stop fragments.

questions.q: Two hours of resolving chest discomfort. Which ECG findings mean immediate transport to the emergency department?
a: A new left bundle branch block
d: Voltage criteria for left ventricular hypertrophy
questions.why: Each of the four raises the likelihood of acute coronary syndrome. The other four are common findings that change nothing about his risk, and a normal ECG a year ago is what makes the bundle branch block new.

questions.q: A T-score of minus 1.9 and incidental thoracic compression fractures. What is the diagnosis?
questions.why: A fragility fracture, one with no trauma or from a fall at standing height or lower, makes the diagnosis osteoporosis regardless of the T-score, and she is treated. Spondylolysis is a pars stress fracture in young athletes; spondylolisthesis is a degenerative slip.

questions.q: What makes a fracture a fragility fracture?
questions.a: No trauma, or a fall from standing height or less
d: Any fracture after the age of 50
A fracture with a T-score below minus 1
A fracture of the hip or wrist specifically
questions.why: The mechanism defines it, not the bone or the scan. T-scores between minus 1.0 and minus 2.49 are osteopenia, and a fragility fracture overrides them.

questions.q: Second-trimester bleeding with a small abruption, no prenatal labs in either pregnancy. Which test matters most now?
questions.why: An Rh-negative woman needs anti-D immunoglobulin now, and after an unmonitored first delivery the risk of fetomaternal mixing is high. The HIV test and cocaine screen have their place but nothing hangs on them today.

questions.q: Which histories justify antiphospholipid antibody testing in pregnancy?
d: Placental abruption in a cocaine user
questions.why: Certain preterm deliveries qualify too. The syndrome is a hypercoagulable state, so the triggers are losses and clots, not bleeding.

questions.q: A needlestick from a patient with active hepatitis B. The nurse was vaccinated years ago and has surface antibody over 10. What is given?
questions.why: A surface antibody above 10 mIU/mL after a completed series is proof of immunity and no prophylaxis is needed. Immune globulin is for the exposed person whose serology is negative.

questions.q: A needlestick from a hepatitis B source in someone with negative hepatitis B serology. What is given?
questions.a: Immune globulin and the vaccine series
d: The vaccine series on its own
Serology again in six weeks, then decide
questions.why: The globulin gives immediate passive protection and the vaccine builds lasting immunity. Immunity from a past infection shows as both core and surface antibody.

questions.q: A fair-skinned 20-year-old at a wellness visit. What does the task force say about skin cancer?
questions.a: Counsel on sun protection; no screening examination
questions.why: Counselling on ultraviolet exposure for fair skin from 6 months to 24 years carries a B recommendation, while the evidence for a screening examination is insufficient.

questions.q: What would make chlamydia screening due for a 20-year-old woman?
questions.why: The B recommendation covers sexually active women under 25. Obesity at 20 earns intensive behavioural weight intervention rather than diabetes screening, which starts at 35.

questions.q: Flashing lights and new floaters in one eye of a 65-year-old, no pain, baseline acuity, a field defect. Diagnosis?
questions.why: Peripheral flashes and floaters are the classic warning, and he needs a dilated examination the same day. Migraine aura is transient and followed by headache, and a first migraine at 65 would need investigating anyway.

questions.q: Which features point to central retinal artery occlusion rather than detachment?
questions.a: Painless sudden loss with a pupillary defect
d: Transient zigzags followed by a headache
Eye pain after a blow to the face
questions.why: The occlusion is ischaemic, so it comes in a patient with vascular risk factors and shows a cherry-red spot on fundoscopy. Pain after trauma raises globe rupture.

questions.q: Two weeks of severe mechanical low back pain, no neurological signs. Which added feature would justify an MRI?
d: Pain that stops him standing straight
questions.why: Retention, bladder fullness and saddle anaesthesia are the cauda equina features that cannot wait. Intravenous drug use raises the chance of an epidural abscess but is not an indication without signs of infection, and pain severity does not track pathology.

questions.q: What does early advanced imaging for low back pain lead to?
questions.why: Imaging finds things that get treated whether or not they cause the pain. Nocturnal pain is common in benign back pain; pain in the second half of the night is the variant worth a second look.
